answer: One idea from jury selection: let both sides of a job strike graders. The panel gets drawn, then the buyer and the seller can each veto three names before grading starts, and those seats get refilled. If a farm wants to swing the review of a trellis repair quote, its clones have to survive the other side's vetoes, and a batch of accounts that all showed up the same week is the first thing anyone strikes. So it needs way more clones than seats, each with a past that doesn't look planted, and every vine disease report or canyon trail survey draws a new panel.
